description.value: This study used functional magnetic resonance imaging to compare brain activation during heroin-related cue exposure in abstinence-based therapy, methadone maintenance therapy, and healthy control subjects.

spans.text: In this study, we addressed this question by using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to identify brain activation in response to heroin-related cues in subjects who have been successfully treated using ABT or MMT and in control subjects.

value: we hypothesized that prefrontal cortex remains particularly overactive in ABT group who are psychologically “trained” to refrain from heroin when compared with MMT group who are pharmacologically helped to lose their interest in heroin.

The task was a pictorial block design consisted of 24 heroin-related stimuli and 24 neutral stimuli that were selected from International Affective Picture System ( Lang et al., 2008 ) and matched on the basis of the object category class.

The task was implemented using the E-prime software package (Psychology Software Tools Inc, Sharpsburg, Pennsylvania) and projected on a white screen in front of the scanner and viewed by a mirror system mounted on the head coil.

stimuli.value: 24 heroin-related stimuli and 24 neutral stimuli selected from the International Affective Picture System.
